ai.description: This slender snake reaches 1.2 meters. It is olive-brown above with a distinct black eye-stripe and a pale yellow or cream ventral surface. A diagnostic feature is the lack of a blue interstitial skin.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Dendrelaphis andamanensis* is best distinguished by the distinct, broad black stripe running along its flanks, which is bordered above by a prominent, vivid white line.
ai.habitat: The Andaman Bronze-back inhabits the dense tropical evergreen and semi-evergreen forests of the Andaman Islands, typically found in low-to-mid-altitude arboreal environments.
ai.behavior: The Andaman Bronze-back is a diurnal, arboreal snake that actively hunts lizards and frogs among the branches of coastal forests and mangroves.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Dendrelaphis andamanensis* is oviparous, laying clutches of 3–6 eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Dendrelaphis andamanensis* is endemic to the Andaman Islands in the Bay of Bengal, occurring from sea level to low-elevation tropical forests.
